objective: Make Brain decide, for each goal, which opportunities to REJECT, HOLD/INVESTIGATE or PRIORITIZE — cheaply, explainably and from the goal's own limits — so research capacity goes to the opportunities and questions most likely to change the goal's outcome, not to listings with large advertised prices. VERIFIED BASELINE (production eeaa539, 2026-10-29): much of this already exists and MUST be extended, not duplicated. server/services/cash/tier.ts (CASH_TIERS SIGNAL/CANDIDATE/QUALIFIED/READY_TO_TEST, SIGNAL_MEANING ~201, cashTier ~319) already says an asking price, appraisal, published rate or solicitation is not a payer. server/services/cash/worthResearching.ts (notWorthResearching ~105, called from validation.ts ~449, operate.ts ~407/~461/~633, monetization/commissionPass.ts ~869) gates research on marketplace listings and closing-before-dive only; its header records that the capital gate was REMOVED on 2026-10-28 because research is reading, not spending — keep that: capital alone may not block research when a no-capital route (pre-sale, brokerage, fee, finder) is plausible. server/services/cash/portfolio.ts (placements ~186, rank ~391, assemble ~622) ranks lexicographically over observable facts with unknowns sorting last — keep that principle; no weighted score, no invented probability. server/services/cash/reconsider.ts reopens pieces on a distinct changeRef. server/services/cash/figures.ts reads money only from sources. server/services/cash/discoveryYield.ts counts which ways of looking pay off. server/services/cash/retireListings.ts already stops research via cancelResearch (server/services/research/queue.ts). server/services/cash/journey/learning.ts (recordOutcomes ~37, cashOutcomeLessons ~234, LESSON_MIN_SAMPLE 3) records outcomes. Goal limits are already stored and read by server/services/goals/target.ts TargetReading: metric (SETTLED_CASH / COLLECTED_CASH / CONTRIBUTION), targetCents, daysLeft, capitalCeilingCents, capitalBeforeProofCents, capitalPerWeekCents, hoursCeiling, resources, proven. The sibling campaign objectives/scenario-expansion.json owns server/services/goals/**, server/services/cash/goalScenario.ts, server/domain/scenario.ts and server/services/scenario/**; this campaign does NOT edit those paths — it produces screened, layered, ranked candidates those planners consume through exported functions. WORK, split by the architect into independently testable units with disjoint owned paths: (A) VALUE LAYERS. On the opportunity/card, store and keep separate: advertised/theoretical value; evidence of completed market transactions; evidence of current buyer demand; evidence this specific opportunity is accessible to us; expected costs and capital; evidence-supported realistic revenue; confirmed commitments and money received (the ledger). Each layer carries its source and VERIFIED / ESTIMATE / UNKNOWN. Only the realistic-revenue layer (and the ledger) may count toward a goal; advertised value, market size, published awards, buyer budgets, resale asking prices and unagreed commissions contribute zero. Reuse figures.ts and the card fact repositories; add nullable columns or a side table only if needed (additive migration). (B) DETERMINISTIC SCREEN, code only, no Claude job. Reads limits from the goal's TargetReading, never hardcoded: capital required vs capitalCeilingCents / capitalBeforeProofCents (REJECT unless a named no-capital route exists, then HOLD with that route as the question); payment timing vs daysLeft for COLLECTED_CASH / SETTLED_CASH goals (payment after the deadline cannot count); stated eligibility/permission requirements vs recorded capabilities and standing exclusions (e.g. no SAM.gov registration, no freelancing); still active / expired; duplicates via duplicates.ts; source freshness. Missing facts never reject and never count as favourable — they produce HOLD with the fact named. Wire it in front of research launch where notWorthResearching is called today, extending that function's reasons rather than adding a parallel gate. (C) DECISION RECORD. One current decision per opportunity per goal: REJECT / HOLD / PRIORITIZE, with reason, binding goal constraint, missing facts, evidence ids, and the condition that would reopen it. Reconsideration goes through reconsider.ts changeRefs (new evidence, changed goal limits, a date passing), never a timer. Nothing is deleted; a person's own archive/decline is never reversed. (D) VALUE OF INFORMATION. Before a research question is launched, decide in code whether any possible answer could change the decision (e.g. payment terms are moot once capital already rejects; payment timing is decisive when an opportunity could cover most of the goal). Questions that cannot change the decision are skipped and recorded as skipped with why; remaining questions are ordered by decision impact vs cost, cheapest factual checks first. Evaluate the whole commercial mechanism (repeatability, volume) not a single listing's size. (E) RANKING. Extend portfolio.ts rank so the criteria order and their meaning come from the goal (metric, deadline, capital limits) and the realistic-revenue layer: goal fit, achievable contribution, time to usable cash, capital, workload/hours, buyer accessibility, demand evidence, delivery feasibility, dependencies, downside, repeatability, combinability, evidence quality. Unknowns still sort last on their criterion; the explanation names the deciding trade-off. (F) LEARNING. Extend journey/learning.ts so every reject / deprioritize / promote / proven / failed outcome records WHY in a small closed vocabulary that separates opportunity failures (CAPITAL_TOO_HIGH, NO_BUYER_FOUND, PAID_TOO_LATE, NOT_ELIGIBLE, EXPIRED, DELIVERY_INFEASIBLE …) from method failures (SOURCE_UNREADABLE, SEARCH_ANGLE_NOISE, RESEARCH_INCONCLUSIVE …). Similar candidates under comparable goal conditions are deprioritized in proportion to measured repeats (at least LESSON_MIN_SAMPLE), never permanently banned, and a changed goal or new method/evidence lifts the effect. (G) BREADTH AND COMBINATIONS. Novel or unseen opportunity types get HOLD/INVESTIGATE, never REJECT for being unfamiliar. The exploit / investigate / explore balance is read from discoveryYield.ts measurements, not a fixed percentage. No per-opportunity minimum revenue: small repeatable opportunities stay eligible and are exported as candidate sets for the scenario planner's combination search. When nothing is supported, discovery keeps running. (H) RESOURCE RELEASE. When an opportunity becomes REJECT or a decision-irrelevant HOLD, its open needs, unlaunched ideas, live missions and packets are released through the existing cancel paths (as retireListings.ts does), so slots return to the queue; never touch EXECUTING-or-later work. (I) EXPLANATION. A plain-language reading on the existing Cash / standing view (client/src/russell/Cash.tsx, CashStanding.tsx and their server view in server/services/cash/view.ts / standingSurface.ts): why rejected, why prioritized, what is missing, what would reopen it, which goal limit binds, what evidence supports it, and what further research would cost. Words, not scores. (J) MEASUREMENT for live verification: counters derived from rows for decisions by type, questions skipped, research released, and Claude jobs avoided by the code screen.
expectedOutcome: On every goal, opportunities carry separated value layers and one explained REJECT / HOLD / PRIORITIZE decision computed from that goal's own stored limits; obvious misfits are rejected in code with zero Claude jobs; decision-irrelevant research questions are skipped and their slots released; ranking reflects realistic revenue and goal constraints rather than advertised value; past outcomes adjust priority without bans; novel types and small repeatable plays stay in play; and on Peyton's stored $10K goal the before/after reading shows large-asking-price listings no longer hold research or rank high, with counts of jobs avoided and slots freed read from rows.
nonGoals: A second ranking or gating module beside portfolio.ts and worthResearching.ts — extend those.
Any weighted composite score, numeric success probability or confidence percentage shown as a measurement.
Hardcoding Peyton's $10K target, deadline, capital ceiling or any other goal's numbers.
Permanently banning a market, category or business model.
Re-adding the pre-2026-10-28 rule that zero deployable capital blocks all research on resale openings.
Editing server/services/goals/**, server/services/cash/goalScenario.ts, server/domain/scenario.ts or server/services/scenario/** (owned by objectives/scenario-expansion.json).
Rebuilding discovery or the research engine; changing what discovery searches for.
Changing authorization, project isolation, credentials, account permissions, spending authority or anything under server/services/identity/**.
Deleting rows, or reversing a decision a person made.
Touching EXECUTING-or-later work when releasing research.

acceptanceConditions.statement: A domain listed at $85,000 with no recorded transaction or buyer evidence contributes $0 of achievable revenue to a goal and does not outrank a supported smaller opportunity.
acceptanceConditions.verification: npm test — behaviour test through the value layers and portfolio rank.

acceptanceConditions.statement: An opportunity requiring capital above the goal's capitalCeilingCents or capitalBeforeProofCents is REJECTed with that limit named, or HOLD only when a named no-capital route exists, and the same opportunity under a goal with a higher ceiling is not rejected for capital.
acceptanceConditions.verification: npm test — two goals, one opportunity.

acceptanceConditions.statement: An opportunity whose payment arrives after the goal's deadline contributes nothing toward a COLLECTED_CASH or SETTLED_CASH goal.
A government award or competitive bid with a large published value and no commitment counts as $0 secured revenue.
A small opportunity with demand and accessibility evidence outranks a much larger one supported only by advertised value.
Several small opportunities that only together reach the goal all survive screening (no per-opportunity minimum) and are exported together as a candidate set for the planner.
An opportunity with a missing payer, price or payment-timing fact is HOLD with that fact listed as missing — never REJECT for the gap, never PRIORITIZE on an assumed value.
After at least LESSON_MIN_SAMPLE recorded failures of the same reason under comparable goal conditions, a similar new candidate ranks lower; under a goal where that reason does not bind, it does not.
New evidence or a changed goal limit reopens a REJECT or HOLD exactly once through a reconsider.ts changeRef and the decision is recomputed.

When an opportunity becomes REJECT, its open needs, unlaunched ideas, missions and packets are released through the existing cancel paths and the slot is free for other work; EXECUTING work is untouched.
An opportunity of a type with no prior history is HOLD/INVESTIGATE, not REJECT.
Obvious rejections (capital, deadline, expired, excluded category, duplicate) create zero research packets, bins or Claude jobs.
acceptanceConditions.verification: npm test — assert row counts unchanged in research tables.

acceptanceConditions.statement: A research question whose every possible answer leaves the decision unchanged is skipped and recorded as skipped with the reason; a decisive question is launched first.
Two goals with different metrics, deadlines and capital limits produce different decisions and orderings over the same opportunity set.
The Cash / standing view shows each important decision in words — reason, binding limit, missing facts, reopen condition, evidence — with no numeric score or percentage.
acceptanceConditions.verification: npm test — component test against rendered document.

acceptanceConditions.statement: Existing suites still pass and the repository typechecks.

rollbackRequirement: Revert the commits. Any migration only adds nullable columns or new tables; no existing row changes meaning, nothing is deleted, and the screen only moves research state through the cancel paths that already exist.
